newsitem.title: VENEZUELA: Venezuela sets 50 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.
newsitem.headline: Venezuela sets 50 bln bolivar TEM auction Wed.

text.p: The Central Bank of Venezuela announced for Wednesday morning a 30 billion bolivar ($62 million) auction of 178-day "monetary stabilization," or TEM, bills with a 23.86 percent coupon.
The bank said it would also offer 10 billion bolivars ($21 million) in 269-day bills with a 24.57 percent coupon, and another 10 billion bolivars of 358-day bills with a 25.29 percent coupon.
Some 35 billion bolivars of TEMs are due to mature on Thursday.

Coupons at the Wednesday auction are up from last week's 140 billion bolivar issue. Then 178-, 269- and 358-day notes carried 21.53, 22.11, and 22.69 percent coupons respectively for effective yields that rose by about 200 basis points.
The weekly TEM bill auctions are the Central Bank's principal tool of monetary policy, used to restrict liquidity and establish a benchmark for wider interest rates.
